newsitem.title: CANADA: Co-Steel shares continue to rally.
newsitem.headline: Co-Steel shares continue to rally.

text.p: Shares in Co-Steel Inc rose on Wednesday in active trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange as the stock continued to rally from lows reached in April after the steelmaker announced a C$125-million bought deal debenture issue.

"The stock is bouncing back to basically the level it was at before the issue was announced, when a lot of people were shorting the stock against debentures," said analyst Greg Misztela at Griffiths McBurney Partners in Toronto.
Co-Steel shares rose 1.00 to 21.50 in turnover of more than 725,000 shares.
Misztela said the Toronto-based steelmaker's balance sheet was expected to improve in the medium term as Gallitin Steel Co, in which Co-Steel has a 50-percent stake, turns to profit.

"I think the market is becoming much more confident that Gallatin is going to start producing profits. That has been a major drag on the company's earnings. With that turnaround, and some strengthening of other ratios, we think the issue is going to look much better than the previous two years," he said.
Analysts said Co-Steel also benefitted from an improvement in the sector, riding the coattails of stocks including IPSCO Inc, which has risen over 10 percent in the last week.
"They've been acting very well. I mean IPSCO is up almost C$4, just over ten percent, in the past week," said Misztela.
IPSCO was up 0.65 to 42.65 in light trade on Wednesday.

"People seem to be liking the steel stocks... maybe in sympathy with the first heat (of steel) at Montpelier at IPSCO's new development in Iowa," said institutional salesman Rolie Bradley at Maison Placements Canada Inc.
Misztela said Co-Steel has been undervalued since its C$125-million bought deal financing of 6.5-percent convertible debentures in early April.

"The stock has been trading below its book value, which is just under C$21. It was really depressed. I think in this market people are looking for some values, and at $20, $21, I think for long-term investors this represents a pretty good value," he said.
